articles.title: Trump urges Senate to pass permanent daylight saving time, blames Tom Cotton for delay
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has blamed Republican Senator Tom Cotton for holding up a plan to make daylight saving time permanent, urging the Senate to act
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has blamed Republican Senator Tom Cotton for holding up a plan to make daylight saving time permanent, urging the Senate to act on legislation that would end the twice-yearly clock change.Trump, in a post on Truth Social early Friday, accused Cotton of blocking the measure “for reasons unknown” and said Americans were “sick and tired” of changing their clocks twice a year. The House passed the bill, known as the Sunshine Protection Act, by a 308-117 vote in July.The push has stalled in the Senate, which adjourned this week and is not expected to return until after the November 3 midterm elections.Reuters reported that Republican Senator John Kennedy said the proposal's prospects were poor, while Republican Senator Rick Scott, a key sponsor, remained confident that it could eventually pass.If approved, the legislation would keep daylight saving time year-round, giving Americans an extra hour of evening daylight in winter. Under the current system, clocks are set back on November 1.Cotton has opposed making daylight saving time permanent, arguing that it would leave winter mornings darker for children going to school and people heading to work. He has also cited concerns for farmers, construction workers and others who begin their day before sunrise.“Many Americans would be forced to start their day in darkness,” Cotton has argued, saying permanent daylight saving time would push winter sunrises later in parts of the country.Supporters of the bill argue that ending the twice-yearly clock change would reduce disruptions linked to changing clocks and provide more daylight during evening hours. Trump has also claimed it could benefit public safety, health, sports and businesses.The US previously experimented with year-round daylight saving time in 1974 as part of an effort to conserve energy. The policy was unpopular and was repealed later that year.For now, the Senate's schedule means the US will continue with its existing system, including the November 1 switch back to standard time. articles.title: Israel’s Supreme Court overturns election panel ban on Arab parties
articles.summary: Court reinstates two Arab lists and Jewish Knesset member Ofer Cassif as Balad leader withdraws after pressure.
articles.body:
Israel’s top court has overturned an election panel’s ban on Arab parties contesting parliamentary elections this month, saying the decision had not met the legal requirements for excluding them, according to Israeli media.

The Supreme Court justices ruled unanimously on Friday to undo the Central Elections Committee’s disqualification of the country’s two main Arab-majority political lists – Ra’am, also called the United Arab List, and the Joint List, which is an alliance of Hadash, Ta’al and Balad.

The decision keeps Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population, in the race after critics accused the committee of double standards ahead of the October 27 Knesset vote.

The court also voted 7-2 to reinstate Ofer Cassif, a sitting Jewish member of the Knesset from the Arab-Jewish Hadash party and an outspoken critic of Israel’s treatment of Palestinians, media reports said.

The two dissenting justices said Cassif backs “armed struggle against the state of Israel”, which is grounds for his disqualification.

In September, the elections committee voted to disqualify the Joint List and Ra’am as parties, as well as Cassif and Sami Abu Shehadeh, head of the Balad party, as individuals.

The Supreme Court has nearly always overruled the committee when it votes to ban candidates.

However, at a hearing on Thursday, Supreme Court President Yitzhak Amit told Abu Shehadeh that a majority of the nine justices favoured disqualifying him from the election.

They gave him until Friday to withdraw, saying that if he did not, he would be disqualified, according to the Israeli Public Broadcasting Corporation.

Abu Shehadeh withdrew from the election after that.

National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, a far-right ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, led the push to bar him over an article written after the Hamas attacks on October 7, 2023. Abu Shehadeh described the attack as “an important historical event” in the piece, but denies supporting it.

Balad said in a statement that a court-ordered removal, rather than a voluntary one, would have had “grave consequences for the country’s political and parliamentary life” as it would set a precedent around the removal of Arab candidates.

The Ra’am party made history after the 2021 election, becoming the first Arab party to join an Israeli government when it took part in a disparate coalition that briefly removed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from power. Most Palestinian citizens of Israel had stayed out of coalition politics until then.

In this election, Ra’am is also fielding a Jewish Zionist candidate for the first time, Yoav Segalovitz, who won popularity in Arab communities for his work to curb crime as deputy minister for internal security.

The election committee’s September vote drew accusations of a double standard, as Palestinian-led parties faced exclusion while parties led by far-right ministers, some of whom have been sanctioned internationally, stayed on the ballot.

Speaking to Al Jazeera on Friday, Abu Shehadeh said he withdrew because he “didn’t have any other choices”.

Although the Supreme Court has restored the Arab parties to the ballot, Abu Shehadeh said the reversal did not make the original disqualifications acceptable.

“In the end, what happened yesterday was a historical catastrophe for democracy, or the very narrow margins of democracy in the State of Israel,” he said. “I was disqualified because I think differently, because I have a different narrative on how to read history, the present, and the future in the place that we live today.”

articles.title: 4 expert-recommended light therapy lamps to boost your winter energy
articles.summary: The best light therapy lamps are from Northern Light Technologies, Carex, Theralite and Verilux. Are light therapy lamps effective? Experts explain.
articles.body: As the sun rises later and sets earlier during fall and winter, odds are you feel sleepier and less motivated compared to other times of year. To some degree, that’s totally normal, says Dr. Alex Dimitriu, founder of Menlo Park Psychiatry and Sleep Medicine. Sunlight regulates our circadian rhythm and other biological clocks, so when there’s less of it, we feel drained. Until the sun returns in the spring, you can replace missing daylight with light therapy lamps. These devices simulate the light of a sunny sky and can help boost your mood, among other benefits, according to experts. Light therapy is one treatment option for those diagnosed with Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD), a type of depression that follows a seasonal pattern and is impacted by daylight hours, says Dimitriu. But anyone experiencing the winter blues may benefit from light therapy. To learn more about these lamps — also commonly referred to as white light boxes, SAD lights, or, ironically, happy lamps — I consulted experts. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best light therapy lamps to shop Northern Light Technologies consulted with an expert — Dr. Michael Terman, founder and president of The Center for Environmental Therapeutics, a nonprofit research and education institution that’s considered an authority on light therapy — about its design, ensuring it offers features proven effective through his research. The light is built with two adjustable legs and an adjustable light panel. Carex’s SAD lamp is designed with a stand that’s height- and angle-adjustable, allowing you to position it so light projects downward, as experts recommend. The lamp blocks UV light, according to Carex, and you can choose between two light settings: One for light therapy and one for general room lighting. Theralite’s light therapy lamp projects light downward and you can adjust the angle of the panel. The lamp has four light settings, and it’s FSA/HSA eligible. Verilux sent me this light therapy lamp to try, and I now use it daily during the winter months. I elevate it on a stack of books and use it while I’m eating breakfast. When I’m done with my 30-minute session, I take the light panel off its detachable stand and place it in a drawer since it stores flat. You can use the lamp vertically and horizontally, and it’s UV-free. How to shop for light therapy lamps The U.S. Food and Drug Administration does not regulate light therapy lamps, and some options are poorly made, limiting their effectiveness, experts warned me. To ensure you’re purchasing a quality SAD lamp, look for those with the following features: Light intensity: Make sure you purchase a light therapy lamp that emits a 10,000 lux illuminance, says Terman. Lux is a measurement of light intensity, and 10,000 lux of light is comparable to ambient daylight. For comparison, typical room lighting ranges from 300 to 500 lux, according to Phillips.Light screen/panel size: Bigger is better when it comes to the size of a lamp’s light panel/screen, says Terman. That’s because you want to create a wide field of light around your face in order to get the full 10,000 lux “dose.” The Center for Environmental Therapeutics recommends a surface area that exceeds 200 sq. in., but this is made complicated by the fact that most at-home light therapy lamps are smaller in size compared to ones you might find in a doctor’s office. With that being said, try to purchase the largest size lamp you can given your space and budget limitations.UV protection: Overexposure to UV light can damage skin and is what we seek to protect skin from when we apply sunscreen. Because of this, it’s important to make sure you buy light therapy lamps designed with built-in UV-filters or that are labeled “UV-free.”Adjustability: Your light therapy lamp should not shoot light upwards into your eyes, and you should never look directly into the light, just like you should never look directly into the sun, says Terman. It’s best to have light come from above and shine down on you, similar to how sunlight does outdoors. Thus, looking for lamps with adjustable heads and stands is important. If your lamp is not adjustable, try stacking books or other objects and placing it on top, angling it toward you as best you can. We also take steps to ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Alex Dimitriu is the founder of Menlo Park Psychiatry and Sleep Medicine and BrainfoodMD. He is double board-certified in psychiatry and sleep medicine.Dr. Michael Terman is the founder and president of the Center for Environmental Therapeutics, and a retired professor of Clinical Psychology in Psychiatry at Columbia University’s College of Physicians and Surgeons. At Columbia, he established a light therapy research lab, which developed a set of non-pharmaceutical measures to treat SAD as well as other light-responsive mental disorders. Dr. Terman also headed one of the original SAD research centers sponsored by the National Institutes of Health, where he introduced the standardized 10,000 lux light therapy method.Dr. Mariana Figueiro is the director of Mount Sinai’s Light and Health Research Center. She’s also a professor of population health science and policy. Why trust NBC Selected? articles.title: Florida Gators, Georgia Bulldogs caught in social media standoff over origins of 'Bloody Tuesday' practice
articles.summary: Jon Sumrall's "Bloody Tuesday" practice ritual sparked a heated debate between Florida Gators and Georgia Bulldogs fans over who coined it first.
articles.body: Things could not be going much better for the Florida Gators to start the Jon Sumrall era. Sumrall and his team are 4-0 with a 24-point beatdown of a top-five Ole Miss team less than one week ago. Recruiting is on fire and the whole program looks like a completely different monster than they did this time a year ago. FLORIDA DROPS IMPRESSIVE OFFENSIVE PERFORMANCE TO PULL OFF MASSIVE WIN OVER NO. 4 OLE MISS A lot of that is due to Sumrall's intensity as a head coach. The 44-year-old first-time SEC coach has taken great pride in returning the edge that has been missing from Gainesville since Urban Meyer exited Alachua County back in December 2010. Just hearing the man talk for more than 60 seconds confirms this, and in keeping with the theme of being an absolute psychopath (in the best way possible, of course), Sumrall is instituting a ritual for his Tuesday practices which will ensure maximum violence and physicality. He's calling it "Bloody Tuesday." FLORIDA COACH JON SUMRALL REVEALS EARLY CAREER STRUGGLES, LIVING IN SLUMS OF SAN DIEGO AND 'CARRYING A GLOCK' "We got a great indoor (practice facility) here," Sumrall said on The Triple Option Podcast. "On Tuesdays, we don’t use the damn indoor. I don’t want anybody going in the indoor on Tuesday. We’re going to be outside. I hope it’s hot. Tuesdays have to be physical and violent, and you gotta strain, or you don’t know how to play way on Saturday." If you're a Gator fan, you have to be pumped hearing that. After years and years of milquetoast scrimmages run by mealy mouthed head coaches, it's refreshing to see Sumrall bringing some much-needed juice back to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. But not everyone is impressed with Sumrall's "Bloody Tuesday," particularly fans of Florida's archrivals, the Georgia Bulldogs. Dawg fans on social media have pointed out that Kirby Smart has been using the term "Bloody Tuesday" to describe his weekday practices since arriving in Athens in 2016. HIGH STAKES, SOCIAL MEDIA BARBS REMIND COLLEGE FOOTBALL FANS THAT AUBURN AND FLORIDA SHARE HISTORY OF HATRED Uh-oh! Is Sumrall guilty of copying Kirby's homework and turning it in as his own? Well, it's a little more complicated than that. As Gator fans were quick to point out, the aforementioned Urban Meyer started calling his Tuesday practices "Bloody Tuesday" all the way back in 2009, and it perhaps dates back to an even earlier period in the Meyer era. Georgia fans responded with articles from 2003 showing that former head coach Mark Richt used the phrase early in his tenure, creating a good old fashioned social media standoff. So who's right here? The truth of the matter is, both of these fanbases are wasting their breath. The term "Bloody Tuesday" isn't some revelatory concept; it's literally an adjective followed by a day of the week. None of these coaches invented the printing press or discovered penicillin, and if you really want to get historical, Richt wasn't even the first one to start using the term "Bloody Tuesday." Not by a long shot. A quick Google search shows that legendary Penn State coach Hugo Bezdek coined the phrase back in the 1920s to describe his physical weekday practices with the Nittany Lions. So, if anyone has a right to be upset with both of these programs, it's the Penn State faithful, though I doubt any of those fans who were alive for Bezdek's reign have an X account to be able to weigh in. Much of coaching football is taking ideas from your predecessors and adopting them as your own with a personal twist. Sumrall likely got the idea from Meyer, and Smart likely got the idea from Richt, who in turn adopted it from legendary Georgia coach Vince Dooley. It's like getting mad at Metallica for using power chords because Black Sabbath did it first. There's plenty of productive things to argue about between these two fanbases, and "Bloody Tuesday" is pretty far down the list. Then again, this is part of what makes college football rivalries so great. Hopefully at their press conferences next week, both Sumrall and Smart pay homage to the true originator of "Bloody Tuesday" so we can all just move on with our lives. articles.title: Sudan’s army says it captured RSF stronghold in North Kordofan
articles.summary: Sudanese Armed Forces reportedly retake al-Mazroub, advancing the army’s goal of cutting the RSF’s supply lines.
articles.body:
The Sudanese Armed Forces say they have taken control of al-Mazroub in North Kordofan state following fierce battles with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), marking a significant gain in one of the war’s main battlegrounds .

In a statement on Friday, the military said fierce battles resulted in casualties among the paramilitary RSF forces, as well as heavy combat vehicle losses.

“The Armed Forces urge citizens in the liberated areas to rest assured and return to their normal lives,” the statement added.

A Sudanese army source told Al Jazeera that al-Mazroub was the RSF’s largest stronghold in North Kordofan.

Army Special Forces spokesman Mohammed Deidan told the Anadolu news agency that the city links the states of North Kordofan and West Kordofan and that, by seizing it, the army was advancing its goal of cutting the RSF’s supply lines.

Fighting in Sudan’s Kordofan region has intensified since late 2025, turning it into one of the main battlegrounds in the war between the army and the RSF, now in its fourth year.

The vast region – which comprises North, West and South Kordofan states – lies where the two sides’ areas of control meet, between the army-held central region and the RSF-controlled Darfur in the West.

Since the war began in April 2023, one in five recorded attacks in Sudan has taken place in Kordofan.

The army has the upper hand in the north, the RSF in the west, and South Kordofan remains contested.

Adding another layer of ethnic friction to the country’s wider civil war, last month the Sudan Doctors Network accused the RSF-allied Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N) of carrying out the artillery attack in the town of Dilling, in the South Kordofan province.

The SPLM-N is a breakaway faction of the SPLM, the governing party of neighbouring South Sudan. Its leader, Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, has aligned his fighters with the RSF and joined ranks with the RSF-led parallel government in Sudan.

articles.title: ‘Pilot may have thought Raja should be removed’
articles.summary: Former Punjab Congress chief Raja Warring resigns, says Sachin Pilot may have wanted him replaced; plans break amid party infighting before 2027 polls.
articles.body: Chandigarh: Former Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Friday indicated that state in charge Sachin Pilot may have been of the view that he should be replaced but made it clear that no discussion took place on the matter between them.“I have been in politics for a long time. I have come up from the grassroots and worked from the block level. I feel that Sachin Pilot may have thought that Raja should be removed. I do not have any concrete evidence for this,” Warring tod the media after submitting his resignation to Rahul Gandhi in New DelhiWarring said he had met Pilot formally only once, for about 15 minutes, to congratulate him after his appointment. Pilot later visited Chandigarh for a two-hour protest, after which, Warring said, “the two of us did not meet again”.On speculation that a rival faction led by former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi had pushed for his removal, Warring dismissed the suggestion of any personal dispute. “Pressure keeps coming and going... That is fine. This is the struggle and this is politics,” he said.Warring, who is learnt to be planning a family holiday abroad, said he intended to take a break and rest after stepping down, following weeks of internal friction within the state unit ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.On his meeting with Gandhi, Warring said, “He gave me a lot of affection and sought information about the situation in Punjab, what was happening, and what we should do. I shared my four years of experience as the state president with him. I told him where our challenges are, how we will have to fight those challenges, and where our strengths lie.”Internal differences had escalated after the Congress leadership reconfirmed Warring as state chief on July 1, prompting opposition from senior leaders aligned with Channi who sought a change in the state leadership.Following his meeting with Gandhi, Warring and his wife offered prayers at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib in New Delhi to express gratitude and seek blessings.Dhillon mocks CongressJP Punjab president Kewal Singh Dhillon took a swipe at the Congress, saying that Warring’s resignation would not resolve the party’s internal problems. “If you think that Raja Warring’s resignation will fix everything in Congress, then you are greatly mistaken.
